title: National Gallery of Armenia: Masterpieces
subtitle: Church interiors, mountain views and painted legends offer different ways of giving a place historical weight.
introduction:
In Sureniants's church interiors, buildings remain after violence has passed through them. Carved stone survives beside bodies or displaced objects. Elsewhere in this selection, a cathedral fills with a procession, an isolated ruin stands open to the sky, and mountains change with the weather.

Place is the connecting thread, but it does different work in each picture. Architecture can bear witness to damage; a landscape can establish distance; a patterned setting can absorb a figure into its colours. The portraits and still lifes offer a smaller scale of attention between these larger views. Together, the twenty-five works show how much can depend on the ground around a subject, rather than on the subject alone.
visitNote: Check the National Gallery's current visitor information and exhibitions before travelling. Armenian and Russian titles can have several English transliterations. The linked records and reproductions will help distinguish a work from another version or a similarly named picture.

books.title: Armenia: Art, Religion, and Trade in the Middle Ages
books.author: Helen C. Evans, editor; The Metropolitan Museum of Art
books.note: An illustrated study of medieval Armenian art, available as a free PDF. Its coverage of churches and religious objects gives background to some of the places and subjects painted here. It is not a catalogue of the modern collection.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by M. T. H. Sadler
books.note: Kandinsky's writing on colour and form, in an English translation. It offers a contemporary artist's arguments to consider beside the early twentieth-century paintings in this guide. It does not establish that their makers followed his ideas.

selectionNote: Artline selected these works from documented museum holdings. The selection is independent of the museum, and individual works may be on loan or off display. Dates and attributions retain the qualifications in the linked records.

works.title: After the Massacre
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. After the Massacre. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The fighting is over. Bodies and scattered objects occupy the floor beneath carefully described carving, leaving a large, emptied volume above them. Sureniants makes aftermath the condition of looking: the architecture remains, but its use has been violently broken. The National Gallery's current exhibition account dates this painting to 1898, rather than the 1899 found in some older records.

works.title: Desecrated Shrine
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. Desecrated Shrine. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Overturned objects disturb the order of a church whose piers and decorated walls remain standing. A shadowed doorway extends the space beyond what can be clearly examined. No central figure explains the violation. The relation between intact architecture and disordered contents makes the damage legible, requiring attention to the setting rather than to an isolated dramatic gesture.

works.title: The Return of Queen Zabel of Armenia
works.catalogueTitle: Return of Queen Zabel of Armenia
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. Return of Queen Zabel of Armenia. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The queen's relatively clear patch of floor sets her apart from the attendants and armed figures crowding either side. Their gestures converge on her without dissolving that separation. Historical costume identifies a distant world, but the immediate encounter depends on spacing: one person remains exposed at the centre of several other people's attention and demands.

works.title: Semiramis at the Body of Ara the Beautiful
works.catalogueTitle: Semiramis at the corpse of Ara the Beautiful
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. Semiramis at the corpse of Ara the Beautiful. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The legendary encounter takes place low in a room that seems to exceed its actors. Semiramis bends toward Ara's body while decorated wall rises above them. That imbalance changes the scale of the event: the central figures are important to the story but occupy only a small part of the image. Architecture gives their isolation a visible measure.

works.title: Portrait of Mkrtich Khrimian
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. Portrait of Mkrtich Khrimian. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A broad area of blue clothing steadies the portrait among plants, carpet and furniture. Khrimian's face and hands emerge from that large shape, while the room supplies a lived setting for his clerical identity. The chair gives his body a formal place, yet the surrounding objects prevent the sitter from becoming only an emblem of office.

works.title: The Procession Leaving Etchmiadzin Cathedral
works.catalogueTitle: The Departure of the Procession from St. Etchmiadzin Cathedral
works.credit: Vardges Sureniants. The Departure of the Procession from St. Etchmiadzin Cathedral. Image credit: Vardges Sureniants. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Faces, banners and vestments collect beneath a portal much taller than the people passing through it. The entrance establishes scale; the crowd gives the building an active social use. Set beside the violated interiors, the difference is substantial. Similar architectural mass can enclose absence in one painting and frame a community's movement in another.

works.title: Ani Cathedral
works.credit: Arshak Fetvadjian. Ani cathedral. Image credit: Arshak Fetvadjian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The roofline opens into the sky, making loss part of the cathedral's silhouette. Warm stone and repeated arches give the remaining structure enough definition to be read as a particular building. The sparse surroundings leave little competing activity. Fetvadjian lets both architectural description and the ruin's isolated position remain visible, without supplying figures to dramatise its condition.

works.title: Mount Ararat from Etchmiadzin
works.credit: Yeghishe Tadevosyan. Mounth Ararat from Ejmiadzin. Image credit: Yeghishe Tadevosian (1870 - 1936). Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A low strip of settlement gives way to the much larger blue mass of Ararat. Tadevosyan keeps the foreground economical, so the mountain's outline becomes the principal organising shape. Its dominance is made pictorially, through size and the scarcity of competing forms. The greenish sky gives the summit a distinct field against which to register.

works.title: Aragats
works.credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Aragats. Image credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Cloud and light break the mountain into changing levels of visibility. Snowy peaks do not remain one continuous emblem; some slopes emerge while others withdraw into shade. Bashinjaghian's view gives weather an active role in describing the place. Compared with Tadevosyan's compact Ararat, it asks the eye to follow conditions across the breadth of a landscape.

works.title: Lake Sevan and Island in the Morning
works.catalogueTitle: Lake Sevan and island in the morning
works.credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Lake Sevan and island in the morning. Image credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The dark shore establishes a near edge before the eye crosses the still water. A small boat helps measure the distance to the island, whose reflection softens its boundary. Almost everything depends on modest tonal changes. The lake feels extensive because its few elements are carefully separated, not because the painting supplies an abundance of detail.

works.title: A Rainy Day at Sevan
works.credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Rainy day in Sevan. Image credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Rain and mist limit the distance that was so available in the morning view. The small sail and low island remain as points of orientation under a much heavier sky. Comparing the two Sevan pictures makes weather more than atmosphere: it changes the information the place offers and the space through which the eye can move.

works.title: Birch Grove
works.credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Birch Grove. Image credit: Gevorg Bashinjaghian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Depth is assembled from repeated trunks rather than a distant landmark. The nearest birch stands apart from smaller trees behind, while dark bark marks interrupt the pale verticals. Sunlight produces further intervals among the leaves. Following those changes in size and spacing allows the grove to open gradually, one tree at a time.

works.title: Mules Laden with Hay
works.credit: Martiros Saryan. Mules, laden with hay. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The loads nearly conceal the animals carrying them. Small dark legs remain beneath large rounded bundles, making the imbalance between burden and bearer the picture's governing proportion. Saryan separates the bright forms clearly against yellow ground. Transport becomes a compact visual problem in weight, repetition and how little of an animal must remain visible for it to be recognised.

works.title: Egyptian Masks
works.credit: Martiros Saryan. Egyptian masks. Image credit: Martiros Saryan; Source credit: https://punto-di-vista.livejournal.com/51051.html. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Faces overlap in shallow space, with eyes and mouths repeated at different scales. The large yellow face anchors one side of the arrangement while colour separates neighbouring forms. The title gives a broad subject, but does not identify each object archaeologically. Saryan's painted relationships can be followed without supplying unsupported origins for every mask.

works.title: Café Pittoresque
works.credit: Georgy Yakulov. Cafe Pittoresque. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Lettering occupies the same ochre field as the standing figure and small animal. It helps compose the sheet instead of waiting below as a caption. Yakulov therefore gives the café a visual identity without presenting a conventional interior view. Reading and looking become neighbouring activities, each requiring a share of the surface.

works.title: Komitas
works.credit: Yeghishe Tadevosyan. Komitas. Image credit: Yeghishe Tadevosyan. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: White clothing separates Komitas from the greens around him. His raised hand and turned head give direction to a tall standing figure, while smaller people continue the landscape behind. The portrait does not isolate its subject from the world. It keeps him identifiable within an environment that has room for other activities and distances.

works.title: Talent and the Crowd
works.credit: Yeghishe Tadevosyan. Talent and the crowd. Image credit: Yeghishe Tadevosyan. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The title proposes a conflict; the interval between one advancing figure and the packed group makes it visible. Faces gather densely behind the darker body in front. That division is the safest starting point for interpretation. It allows the painting to address an individual's relation to collective pressure without requiring an invented historical incident to explain it.

works.title: The Courtyard of Sanahin Monastery
works.credit: Panos Terlemezyan. Sanahin monastery courtyard. Image credit: Panos Terlemezyan. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Separate patches of light reveal enough stone to suggest the surrounding vaults and columns. Much remains in shadow, so the space must be assembled across interruptions. Terlemezyan's inward view differs from the exposed silhouette at Ani. Here, enclosure is experienced through partial access to surfaces rather than through a complete architectural outline.

works.title: A Shepherd from Lori
works.credit: Panos Terlemezyan. Shepherd from Lori. Image credit: Panos Terlemezyan. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Fur hat, belt and layered clothes identify the sitter through particular material things. His low hands leave the face and upper body carrying most of the encounter. The dark interior limits distraction without turning the shepherd into an anonymous type. Close description gives a working man's appearance the space usually granted to a formal portrait.

works.title: Still Life with Vegetables
works.credit: Hmayak Hakobyan. Still Life. Vegetables. Image credit: Hmayak Hakobyan. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Each vegetable meets light differently. Rounded skin, cut surfaces and green stalks distinguish objects that overlap closely before a dark ground. Hakobyan makes their contact convincing through those differences: one rests against another, one edge interrupts the next. The still life offers a smaller-scale counterpart to the architectural pictures' attention to material surfaces.

works.title: Still Life: Plums
works.credit: Zakar Zakarian. Still life. Plums. Image credit: Zakar Zakarian. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Only part of each object is sharply available. A glint describes a curve, then an edge disappears into the brown surroundings. Zakarian leaves the eye to join those fragments into fruit and vessels. The slower emergence of form contrasts with Hakobyan's more distinctly separated vegetables, despite the two paintings' closely related domestic subjects.

works.title: Seascape
works.credit: Vartan Mahokian. Seascape. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The horizon stays level while the nearer water breaks in competing directions. Pale foam separates the crests from the darker green beneath, making movement legible without a ship or coastal landmark. Mahokian distributes variation across a stable underlying view. The waves can differ because the distant boundary gives them something steady to move against.

works.title: The Siege of Kazan
works.credit: Nicholas Roerich. Siege of Kazan. Image credit: Nicholas Roerich. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Roerich compresses people and fortifications into overlapping bands beneath large red and pink clouds. The sky takes on as much visual weight as the historical action below. Strong pattern gives the scene something of a theatrical arrangement. It offers an interpretation of the siege, rather than the kind of spatial account from which its movements could be reconstructed.

works.title: The Way of Giants
works.credit: Nicholas Roerich. Way of giants. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/nicholas-roerich/way-of-giants-1914
works.description: The giants remain in the title. In the picture, interlocking blue rocks and a curling sky provide the legendary scale. Firm outlines keep the terrain unusually emphatic, while the forms above it flow. The contrast allows a landscape without visible protagonists to carry the expectation of a story through colour, solidity and proportion.

works.title: Woman in a Blue Dress
works.credit: Victor Borisov-Musatov. Woman in Blue Dress. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Patterns on the dress continue the activity of surrounding leaves and flowers. The figure partly joins that decorative field, while face and hands remain clearer points of orientation. Borisov-Musatov allows person and setting to share a surface without making them identical. The spreading skirt gives the lower part of the composition its broadest connection between body and design.

closingSections.title: Return to an empty interior
paragraphs: After the landscapes and portraits, the opening churches may seem less like backgrounds and more like subjects in their own right. Compare what survives, what has moved, and where people can still gather. The selection describes recorded works, not a permanent hanging; confirm access and current display with the gallery before visiting.
